need.summary: Represent the strategy chapters of Bill Gates's 'How to Avoid a Climate Disaster' with traced, open-licence data from primary producers: (1) net-zero targets and the share of emissions they cover; (2) electricity's share of final energy; (3) operating carbon capture and direct air capture; (4) public energy RD&D and clean-energy venture funding; (5) clean electricity standards, low-carbon fuel standards, green public procurement; (6) adaptation finance, smallholder farms, CGIAR, crop yield losses; (7) which Systems Change Lab indicators map to Gates's sectors and levers.
need.rules: Licence from the producer's own terms, quoted verbatim with URL and date. Classes open, share-alike, noncommercial usable; no-derivatives and display-only cannot enter data/; anything built on IEA World Energy Balances is no-derivatives; third-party material inside open products is excluded. Hosts that block scripts are recorded for manual download, never worked around.
need.method: Three research passes (net-zero and policy; electrification, capture and RD&D; adaptation) by curl and web search on 2026-10-08, plus a fresh Systems Change Lab export parsed locally. No repo file other than this one was changed.

The site is the producer's own terms page, and the Zenodo deposit is the producer's own too (its depositors led the database update, and the Stocktake report links to it). 2) The CSV is cp1252-encoded. My test shares for 2023 (China 39.5%, US 22.4%, Germany 20.8%, India 18.8%) depend on those choices and are not a validated method. The derivation would be a pipeline transform, never done in web/.

[net-zero/policy] Climate Watch net-zero licence: its metadata says CC BY-NC 4.0 but links to CC BY 4.0. Only worth asking WRI if we decide to use it.

[electrification/capture/RD&D] Is the registered UNSD source too IEA-based? UNSD's metadata says data for OECD and EU countries come 'through the IEA' and that older data 'may have been imported from the IEA World Energy Statistics Database'. About 150 country entries cite IEA World Energy Statistics. Should unsd-energy stay noncommercial, be limited to countries whose metadata names only UNSD or national sources, or be reclassified?

[electrification/capture/RD&D] How should a UNSD share be derived, if at all? It needs summing fuels in the pipeline, dropping the 0100/0200 coal aggregates and the 5212/5222/5232 'of which' codes, and settling whether blended biofuels sit inside motor gasoline and diesel. Should that be written up with UNSD's balance rules first, or should only Eurostat's published share be used?

[electrification/capture/RD&D] Can the IEA explorers be used when their products are not CC? The RD&D explorer page says 'Licence CC BY 4.0', but the RD&D product says 'Terms of Use for Non-CC Material'. The CCUS explorer and product both say CC BY 4.0, so only RD&D conflicts. The registry accepted the same split for EVs.

[electrification/capture/RD&D] Does the State of CDR licence cover its CDR.fyi-based values? Some 2025 novel-removal values come from CDR.fyi, whose terms forbid republishing. Asking socdr@smithschool.ox.ac.uk would settle it.
